increments.title: A shared-only entry is no candidate for the mandatory auto-add
increments.goal: A fresh roster over a catalogue whose mandatory-looking entry lives only in `sharedSelectionEntries` gets no selection of it at force level, while mandatory rules declared at the catalogue root keep being set automatically and the entry stays choosable where the catalogue offers it.
criteria: An entry that a catalogue holds only in `sharedSelectionEntries` is no candidate for the mandatory auto-add, however its constraints read: a fresh roster over such a catalogue gets no selection of that entry at force level. Pin it on an inline fixture that mirrors the real shape — the entry in `sharedSelectionEntries` with `type="upgrade"`, no own sub-options, `min=1 scope="roster" includeChildSelections="true"`, offered through a shared group a character links — and name `Pure of Heart` / `Honours` in a comment. verify: `npx vitest run src/roster/listRules src/hooks/useRoster`

A mandatory list rule declared at the catalogue root is still set automatically, in both root forms: as a root `selectionEntry`, and as a root `entryLink` whose target is a shared entry carrying the `min`. verify: `npx vitest run src/hooks/useRoster.mandatoryAutoAdd src/hooks/useRoster.costedMandatoryAutoAdd` stay green, plus a new case for the root-`entryLink`-onto-shared-target form.
The entry stays choosable where the catalogue does offer it: on a character that links the group holding it, the option is offered and can be taken. verify: `npx vitest run src/roster`
The JSDoc of `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` states the rule and names ADR 0032, so the write model and the engine read the same on this point.
increments.note: The load-bearing slice: it changes what the auto-add may reach, and both guard criteria (root forms still auto-added, the entry still choosable on a character) exist only to bound that one change, so they are judged with it.

## The change

One production edit, in `src/roster/listRules.js`, function `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` (line 193): drop `...(catalogue.sharedSelectionEntries || []),` from the `pools` array (lines 198-202), so the sweep reads only `catalogue.selectionEntries` and `catalogue.entryLinks`. Nothing else in the function moves: the `isListRuleEntryKind` / `isUnconditionalMandatoryListRule` / hidden / already-present filters, the dedup by `resolved.id`, the visibility context built from `computeRosterCounts`, and the returned `{ entry, resolved, categoryId }` shape all stay exactly as they are.

That single line is the whole fix. `Pure of Heart` (`d0ce-b0c4-fcc1-6cac`) stands in `sharedSelectionEntries` of `High Elves (6th definitive edition).cat` and is offered only through the shared group `Honours` (`45a3-3e65-6c49-5cc0`), which character entries pull in by `entryLink`. With the shared pool gone it is never a candidate, so the auto-add effect in `src/hooks/useRoster.js` (the `useEffect` at lines ~208-231, gated on `isFreshRoster`) creates no selection for it.

## What each root shape does after the change

- **Root `selectionEntry`** (the `Allow experimental rules?` / `Who Is the general?...` shape of issues 0138/0140): still in `catalogue.selectionEntries`, untouched.
- **Root `entryLink` onto a shared target**: still in `catalogue.entryLinks`. `resolveEntry` (`src/roster/catalogResolver.js:276-302`) spreads the target over the link and concatenates the target's `constraints`, so the resolved object carries the target's `type="upgrade"` and its `min`, and `isContainerListRule` sees the target's (absent) children. Every filter therefore still fires. **This form gets strictly better**: today the root link *and* the shared target both pass the sweep and both are added, because the dedup key is `resolved.id` and for a link `resolveEntry` deliberately keeps the *link's* id (line 285), not the target's — so the two never collide in `seenResolvedIds`. After the change exactly one selection is created, built from the root link.

## The JSDoc (criterion 4)

The doc block above `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` (lines 169-192) currently states the pools are "dieselben, die {@link collectPrimaryCategoryEntries} durchläuft: `selectionEntries`/`entryLinks`/`sharedSelectionEntries`". That parity ends with this change and the sentence must go, or the file states something false. Replace it with a block that says:

- The sweep reads the two root pools `selectionEntries` and `entryLinks` only.
- `sharedSelectionEntries` is deliberately excluded: a shared definition is reachable only through a reference and is an offering only at the place of that reference, never at the catalogue root — so it is no candidate for the force-level auto-add, however its own constraints read (a `min=1 scope="roster" includeChildSelections="true"` on such an entry says "one selection of it must exist somewhere in the army", not "the force holds it loose at its root").
- The clean-room engine holds the same rule, so the two models now read alike: ADR 0032 (name it explicitly, per the criterion), realised in `collectRootDefinitions` and `collectArmyLevelCandidates` in `src/evaluator/resolver.js` (lines 130-185), which follow `children` only and never the resolved link target. Note when writing this: ADR 0032's own prose does not spell the rule out in these words — the resolver's JSDoc is where it is written down, so cite both, ADR first.
- A root `entryLink` whose target is a shared entry keeps working, because the filters run on the *resolved* entry.
- Name issue 0153 and `Pure of Heart` as the case, in the style the surrounding blocks use for issues 0138/0140.

## Rejected

- **Filter by reachability instead of by pool** (walk every reference in the catalogue and drop a shared entry that is referenced from a group): rejected — costly, and it answers a question nobody asked. The pool an entry stands in *is* the rule; that is exactly what the engine does.
- **Tighten `isUnconditionalMandatoryListRule`** (e.g. reject a `min` carrying `includeChildSelections="true"`): rejected — criterion 1 says the entry is no candidate "however its constraints read". A constraint-shape filter would also change the verdict for root-declared rules that happen to carry the same attributes.
- **Also drop the shared pool from `collectPrimaryCategoryEntries`** (`src/roster/entryVisibility.js:167-193`): rejected — out of scope. That pool feeds the "+"-adder, `RosterCategorySection.jsx` and the list-rule checklist rows; no criterion of this increment speaks about them. Leave it alone; the checklist/lock question is the later increment's.
- **Touch `src/evaluator/`**: the issue puts it out of scope, and it already holds the rule.

- `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` is re-exported through `src/roster/index.js:24`; `src/hooks/useRoster.js:9` imports it from there. Its only production caller is the auto-add effect in `useRoster.js:216`.

- JSDoc in `src/roster/listRules.js` is German throughout; keep the new block German (see rulings).

return.testPlan:
## Whether

Tests. The change is a behaviour change in a pure function that the roster write model and the fresh-roster effect both read.

## What

### Criterion 1 — a shared-only entry is no candidate for the mandatory auto-add

- **C1** — criterion 1 — an inline catalogue whose only mandatory-looking entry sits in `sharedSelectionEntries` (`type="upgrade"`, no `selectionEntries`/`entryLinks`/`selectionEntryGroups` of its own, constraints `max=1 scope="roster"`, `max=1 scope="parent"`, `min=1 scope="roster" includeChildSelections="true" includeChildForces="true"`), reachable only through a group in `sharedSelectionEntryGroups` whose `entryLinks` point at it, that group linked from a root character `selectionEntry` by an `entryLink` of `type="selectionEntryGroup"`; swept with an empty force → `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections(system, catalogue, emptyForce())` returns `[]`. A comment names `Pure of Heart` (`d0ce-b0c4-fcc1-6cac`) and `Honours` (`45a3-3e65-6c49-5cc0`) out of `High Elves (6th definitive edition).cat`, as the criterion demands. — break: restoring `...(catalogue.sharedSelectionEntries || [])` to the `pools` array of `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections`.
- **C2** — criterion 1 — a fresh roster (`buildRoster`, `isFreshRoster` passed `true`) over a synthetic catalogue XML of that same shape, driven through `useRoster` with nothing mocked → `result.current.roster.forces[0].selections` holds no selection referring to the shared honour, by either its own id or a link to it. — break: the same restore.

### Criterion 2 — a root-declared mandatory rule is still set automatically

- **C3** — criterion 2, root `selectionEntry` form — already pinned by the existing cases in `src/roster/listRules.mandatoryPredicate.test.js` (a root `selectionEntry`, `type="upgrade"`, `min=1 scope="force"`, no children → one hit) and end to end by `src/hooks/useRoster.costedMandatoryAutoAdd.test.js`. No new case; both suites must stay green. — break: dropping `catalogue.selectionEntries` from the sweep's pools.
- **C4** — criterion 2, root `entryLink` form — an inline catalogue holding the mandatory entry (`type="upgrade"`, no children, `min=1 scope="roster"`) in `sharedSelectionEntries` **and** a root `entryLink` in `catalogue.entryLinks` pointing at it; swept with an empty force → exactly one hit (`missing.length === 1`, the repeat edge: not two), and `missing[0].entry` is the root link (it carries `targetId` = the shared entry's id). — break: dropping `catalogue.entryLinks` from the pools, or reading the pool entries without `resolveEntry` so the target's `type`/`min` are never seen. The length assertion additionally fails if the shared pool comes back, since link and target dedup separately (`resolveEntry` keeps the link's own id).
- **C5** — criterion 2, production seam — the synthetic catalogue of C2, extended by a second shared entry that carries `min=1 scope="roster"` and a root `entryLink` onto it → the fresh roster carries exactly one force-level selection, and it is the root-linked one, not the honour. — break: as C4; also fails with two selections if the shared pool returns.

### Criterion 3 — the entry stays choosable where the catalogue offers it

- **C6** — criterion 3 — an inline catalogue with a character `selectionEntry` that links the shared `Honours` group, that group linking the shared honour; `getUnitOptions(system, catalogueId, { selectionEntryId: characterId, selections: [] })` → the result contains an item whose `option.targetId` is the shared honour's id and whose `groupName` is `Honours`; feeding that item's `option` into `createSelectionFromDef({ system, resolveEntry, catalogueId, entry: option })` with the real `resolveEntry` from `catalogResolver.js` yields a selection named `Pure of Heart` carrying `entryLinkId` = the link's id ("and can be taken"). — break: the over-broad version of this fix — making the shared pools unreachable to resolution (`indexEntriesById`/`findEntryInSystem` skipping `sharedSelectionEntries`/`sharedSelectionEntryGroups`), or removing the `EntryLinkKind.SELECTION_ENTRY_GROUP` recursion in `optionsCollector.collectOptions`.

### Left untested, on purpose

- **Criterion 4 (the JSDoc)** carries no case: no test can check that a comment states a rule and names ADR 0032. A grep-for-the-string test would pin wording, not meaning, and would go red on the first rewording. It is checked by reading in review.
- The checklist rows and the mandatory lock (`buildListRuleStates`, `ListRuleChecklist.jsx`) get no case here: nothing in them changes this increment, and the removal-by-hand question is a later increment's.

## How

- **C1, C4** — unit — `src/roster/listRules.mandatoryPredicate.test.js` (existing; append one `describe` for issue 0153 beside the 0138/0140 blocks) — vitest — `npx vitest run src/roster/listRules.mandatoryPredicate.test.js`.
- **C6** — unit — `src/roster/optionsCollector.sharedHonourGroup.test.js` (new file) — vitest — `npx vitest run src/roster/optionsCollector.sharedHonourGroup.test.js`.
- **C2, C5** — integration (the hook over the real parser, the real sweep and the real selection factory) — `src/hooks/useRoster.sharedOnlyMandatory.test.js` (new file) — vitest + `@testing-library/react` (`renderHook`, `act`) — `npx vitest run src/hooks/useRoster.sharedOnlyMandatory.test.js`.
- **C3** — no file, no edit: `src/roster/listRules.mandatoryPredicate.test.js`, `src/hooks/useRoster.mandatoryAutoAdd.test.js` and `src/hooks/useRoster.costedMandatoryAutoAdd.test.js` cover it as they stand.

Both suite docs exist — `src/roster/CLAUDE.md` and `src/hooks/CLAUDE.md` — they cover every convention these three files need, and nothing I read contradicts them, so no correction is due. They are the source for the conventions; two points worth knowing before opening them: `src/roster` test titles are German and its fixtures are inline schema-shaped object literals, while `src/hooks` titles are English and a production-seam `useRoster` file builds its catalogue as XML and parses it with `processImportedData`, then builds the roster with `buildRoster`. `src/hooks/useRoster.costedMandatoryAutoAdd.test.js` is the template for the new hooks file — same synthetic-but-shape-faithful catalogue XML, same `isFreshRoster: true`.

## What counts as done

- `npx vitest run src/roster`
- `npx vitest run src/hooks/useRoster`

Nothing else. `npm ci` first, since the checkout has no `node_modules`.

## What is already red

Unknown, and deliberately so: no decision in this plan turned on a fact only a run could settle. Every shape it rests on was settled by reading — the sweep's pools (`listRules.js:198-202`), the link merge in `resolveEntry` (`catalogResolver.js:276-302`), the whole-graph id index (`indexEntriesById`, `catalogResolver.js:39`), the group-link recursion in `optionsCollector.collectOptions` (line 154), and the fact that the two checklist test files mock `entryVisibility.js` rather than the sweep. The list above is therefore unrun; its first run belongs to whoever runs it downstream.
breaks: An entry that a catalogue holds only in `sharedSelectionEntries` is no candidate for the mandatory auto-add — restoring `...(catalogue.sharedSelectionEntries || [])` to the `pools` array of `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` in `src/roster/listRules.js`.

A mandatory list rule declared at the catalogue root is still set automatically, in both root forms — dropping `catalogue.selectionEntries` or `catalogue.entryLinks` from those same pools, or reading a pool entry without `resolveEntry` so a root link never shows its shared target's `type` and `min`.

The entry stays choosable where the catalogue does offer it — making the shared pools unreachable to resolution (`indexEntriesById`/`findEntryInSystem` in `src/roster/catalogResolver.js` skipping `sharedSelectionEntries`/`sharedSelectionEntryGroups`), or removing the `EntryLinkKind.SELECTION_ENTRY_GROUP` recursion in `collectOptions` (`src/roster/optionsCollector.js:154`).
unbreakable: The JSDoc of `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` states the rule and names ADR 0032 — no test can check that a comment states a rule; a test grepping for the string would pin wording rather than meaning and would go red on the first rewording, so this one is checked by reading in review.
rulings: Pin criterion 1 at both levels — one unit case on the sweep and one production-seam case in a new `src/hooks/useRoster.sharedOnlyMandatory.test.js` — because the criterion is worded as a roster-level observable while its fixture requirement is the src/roster inline style, and the criterion's own verify names both directories; wrong costs one redundant test file.

Write the new JSDoc block of `findMissingMandatoryListRuleSelections` in German, because every JSDoc block in `src/roster/listRules.js` is German and the project's docs rule keeps prose German while identifiers stay English; wrong costs re-translating one comment block.

Cite both ADR 0032 and the resolver's `collectRootDefinitions`/`collectArmyLevelCandidates` in that JSDoc, because ADR 0032's own text never spells the shared-entries rule out in words — the resolver's JSDoc is where it is written down; wrong costs one extra reference in a comment.

Leave the `sharedSelectionEntries` pool in `collectPrimaryCategoryEntries` (`src/roster/entryVisibility.js:174`) untouched, because no criterion of this increment speaks about the category adder or the checklist rows; wrong costs the shared honour still being listed at contingent level, which the later increment on the lock takes up anyway.

Give criterion 3 its own new file `src/roster/optionsCollector.sharedHonourGroup.test.js` instead of extending the module-level fixture of `optionsCollector.test.js`, because the suite doc puts a one-topic case in `<module>.<topic>.test.js`; wrong costs moving one file.

Hold the check list to the two vitest patterns and leave lint, typecheck and the full suite out, because criterion 6 belongs to the increment that ships the fix; wrong costs one late lint failure on a comment-only edit.
return.summary: The fix is one line: the mandatory-list-rule sweep in `src/roster/listRules.js` stops reading `catalogue.sharedSelectionEntries`, so a shared honour like `Pure of Heart` — reachable only through the `Honours` group a character links — is no longer auto-added to a fresh roster, while root `selectionEntry` and root `entryLink` forms keep working (and the link form stops being added twice). Five test cases across two new files and one existing one pin the three testable criteria; the JSDoc criterion is prose and is checked by reading.
